newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan, PLO in joint tourism appeal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan, PLO in joint tourism appeal.

text.p: Israel, the Palestinian Authority and Jordan have joined forces in urging Americans to visit the holy land in an advertisement that follows last week's U.S.-brokered peace deal on Hebron.
"Peace, it's a beautiful sight to see," read the advertisment released to the media on Monday by Israel's Tourism Ministry.
A ministry spokeswoman said the advertisement would run soon in major U.S. newspapers and marked the first such joint initiative taken by the three sides.
"We are all committed to peace," said the ad signed by the Israeli, Palestinian and Jordanian ministries of tourism.

"Today, Israelis, Jordanians and Palestinians open their arms and their hearts to extend a warm invitation to the American people to visit these lands which have given birth to so much faith and so much history," it said.
The Israel Hotel Association said tourists from the United States dropped six percent to 425,000 last year compared with 1995.

It attributed the decline to suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel last February and March and Israeli-Palestinian violence that erupted in September after the opening of another entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israeli tourism industry officials said they now hope that the Hebron agreement will usher in a period of reduced political tensions.
